process_observations.observation: build_plan.py refused nothing this run: next returned the step, running and built both applied cleanly, and check-outputs gated built exactly as § 5 describes rather than trusting the agent's own word.
The owning agent is build-aware (39 hits on the Step 4 probe), so no Step 7 relocation was needed and every artefact landed on the path the plan declared without the runner moving anything.

deploy-order.md is written unconditionally by the owning agent's Step 7 and is absent from the step's outputs[], so it reaches the human as an undeclared artefact and check-outputs never adjudicates it — the W8 remedy is a one-line plan edit the runner may not make.

The step's first acceptance test carries a description asserting a specific checker output ('WARN: 1 finding(s) detected') as well as an expected exit code; the artefact as built produces 2 findings and still exits 0, so the test passes while its description is now wrong — a shape where a passing test carries a false statement.

The artefact's formula and plan.json.steps[].inputs.errorConditionFormula now disagree, and the only CLI writer that could reconcile them — amend-step — is outside this agent's mandate, so the divergence survives into the tester and the doc keeper unless a human acts on it.

The invocation's 'write only under the build dir' constraint and the Wave 10 persistence clause in both AGENT.md files point opposite ways on docs/reports/<agent-id>/; the constraint was honoured and the report pair was not written for either agent.
The step is built and its four acceptance tests have not run.
